$comment: Kanban MVP schema. Target engine: SQLite. IDs are app-generated TEXT strings (not autoincrement integers) so they can keep the frontend's existing prefixed-id convention (col-*, card-*) end to end with no translation layer.

tables.name: users
tables.description: One row per person who can sign in. The MVP only ever seeds a single row ('user'), but the schema supports more from day one.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Internal id, never exposed to the frontend.

columns.name: password_hash
columns.description: Argon2id hash (argon2-cffi), read by /api/login and written by /api/signup as of Part 11. No plaintext or unsalted hash is ever stored.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, SQLite's default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP format.

tables.name: boards
tables.description: A Kanban board belonging to a user. As of Part 12, a user can have any number of boards (the original UNIQUE constraint on user_id was dropped via a guard-function migration in db.py, not a migration tool — see DATABASE.md).

columns.name: name
columns.description: Added in Part 12 via an additive ALTER TABLE guard. User-editable display name shown in the board switcher.

tables.name: columns
tables.description: Ordered, renameable Kanban columns belonging to a board.

columns.name: id
columns.description: App-generated, matches the frontend's existing 'col-*' convention.

columns.name: position
columns.description: 0-based display order among the board's columns. Replaces the frontend's implicit array order.

columns.name: id
columns.description: App-generated, matches the frontend's existing 'card-*' convention.

columns.name: position
columns.description: 0-based display order within the card's column. Replaces the frontend's cardIds array order. Moving a card between columns updates column_id and reassigns position.

relationships: users 1--many boards (as of Part 12; a user may have any number of boards)

frontend_mapping.BoardData.columns[]: SELECT * FROM columns WHERE board_id = ? ORDER BY position
frontend_mapping.BoardData.cards (Record<id, Card>): SELECT * FROM cards WHERE column_id IN (board's columns), keyed by id
frontend_mapping.Column.cardIds[]: cards for that column_id, ORDER BY position, mapped to their ids
